A rare genetic mutation called pseudo-melanism has resulted in roughly half of the tigers in India's Similipal Tiger Reserve sporting coats with far more black than those of usual tigers. This widespread coloration is a symptom of a shallow gene pool in a region that previously faced a dwindling tiger population, and could prove catastrophic if conservation officers aren't able to find these tigers more genetically diverse mates. videos.caption: Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.
